n: Micah laments that searching for a good person is like looking for fruit after the harvest — nothing left but disappointment.

f.w: grapegleanings
f.g: The few grapes left after the harvesters pass through.

f.w: firstripe fruit

n: Faithful people have vanished. Everyone lies in wait to harm others, hunting even their own relatives with nets.

f.w: The good man is perished out of the earth

n: Officials and judges demand bribes, and powerful people get whatever they want. They all scheme together.

f.w: so they wrap it up

n: The best of them is like a briar or thorn hedge — they only hurt. But the day the watchmen warned about is coming, and confusion will seize them.

f.w: thy watchmen
f.g: The prophets who warned of judgment.

f.w: visitation

n: Society is so broken you can’t trust friends, advisers, or even your spouse.

f.w: keep the doors of thy mouth

n: Families are torn apart — children against parents. Jesus quoted this verse to describe how His gospel would divide some households.

f.w: a man's enemies are the men of his own house

n: But Micah turns from despair to faith: “As for me, I will look to the Lord and wait for the God who saves me. My God will hear me.” A turning point for any discouraged heart.

f.w: I will look unto the LORD
I will wait for the God of my salvation

n: Speaking for Zion, Micah tells the enemy not to gloat: “When I fall, I will rise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord will be my light.” Hope survives defeat.

f.w: when I fall, I shall arise
the LORD shall be a light unto me

n: Zion accepts the Lord’s discipline because she has sinned, but trusts He will later take up her cause and bring her into the light. Repentance includes owning our sins and trusting His justice.

f.w: I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned
he will bring me forth to the light

n: The enemy who mocked, “Where is your God?” will be shamed and trampled like mud in the streets.

f.w: Where is the LORD thy God?

n: A day is coming to rebuild Jerusalem’s walls, and its borders will be extended far.

f.w: the decree be far removed

n: In that day God’s people will stream back from Assyria, Egypt, and everywhere — from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.

f.w: the fortified cities
he shall come even to thee

n: Yet first the earth will be desolate because of the deeds of its inhabitants.

f.w: the fruit of their doings

n: Micah prays: Lord, shepherd Your people with Your staff. Let them graze again in the rich pastures of Bashan and Gilead, as in the old days.

f.w: Feed thy people with thy rod
Bashan and Gilead
f.g: Fertile grazing lands east of the Jordan, lost to Assyria.

n: The Lord answers: as when I brought you out of Egypt, I will show you wonders again. The Exodus is the pattern for future deliverance.

f.w: According to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt

n: The nations will be stunned and humbled when they see God’s power. They will cover their mouths, speechless.

f.w: lay their hand upon their mouth

n: Proud nations will crawl in the dust like snakes, trembling as they come out of hiding to submit to the Lord.

f.w: lick the dust like a serpent

n: Micah’s closing hymn plays on his own name (“Who is like Jehovah?”): Who is a God like You, who forgives sin and delights in mercy? God’s anger is temporary; His love is lasting.

f.w: Who is a God like unto thee
f.g: An echo of Micah’s name, Mi-ka-yah, “Who is like Jehovah?”

f.w: he delighteth in mercy

n: God will again have compassion; He will trample our sins underfoot and hurl them into the depths of the sea — gone forever. A beautiful picture of complete forgiveness through the Atonement.

f.w: subdue our iniquities
f.g: Tread them under foot, like conquered enemies.

f.w: cast all their sins into the depths of the sea

n: God will keep the promises He made to Abraham and Jacob long ago. Micah ends with confidence in God’s covenant faithfulness.

f.w: the mercy to Abraham
perform the truth
